question: Following worrying revelations emerging from a media enquiry, which included investigations within the European Parliament itself, it has been shown that some farms that have benefited from EU funding were not in compliance with the set rules at the point in time they received that funding.

The funding has been shown to have been put to unlawful uses, including intensive farming and the mistreatment of animals, in grave contravention of the Animal Welfare Directive and EU legislation.1 The CAP was designed to support the agricultural sector. However, it seems that only a fraction of the investment is reaching small producers, resulting in the closure of many farms across Europe.
Agriculture lies at the heart of the local economy and is key to the preservation of regional identity in southern Italy and across Europe. In view of the above, will the Commission: 1.
Launch an in-depth investigation into the use of agricultural funding to ensure that this is taken up in a manner compliant with EU rules?
Revise funding allocation policies to ensure that these prioritise SMEs, thus supporting biodiversity, production quality and the preservation of regional identities?
Take steps to cut the red tape that is stifling small producers, thereby facilitating their access to funding and allowing them to continue to operate in a traditional and sustainable manner?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.4.2024) In possible cases of fraud, corruption or any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the Union, the Commission refers the matter to the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF). Cases of suspected criminal conduct in respect of which the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) could exercise its competence are then transmitted to the EPPO.

Member States are implementing the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in shared management, respecting rules set at EU level in particular Article 59 of Regulation (EU) 2021/21161. The Commission is conducting risk-based systems audits to ensure that management and control systems put in place are adequate to ensure the intended use of CAP funds.

The latest CAP reform considerably reinforced redistribution of income support towards smaller farms and 32% of CAP funding is used to fund actions for environment, climate and animal welfare. There are also interventions to promote quality schemes.

The current legal framework already provides Member States a large enough leeway to efficiently determine which combination of interventions will achieve sought results, taking into account territorial specificities. Accordingly, the Commission sees no need to revise support policies at this stage.

The Commission is rolling out a wide range of actions to simplify rules, including a modification of the CAP Strategic Plan Regulation adopted on 15 March 20242. easing control and sanctions for small farms.

financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1306/2013 - OJ L 435, 6.12.2021, p. 187. 2 COM (2024) 139 final in legislative procedure.
